newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana carrier opposes new Comair-BA franchise.
newsitem.headline: Botswana carrier opposes new Comair-BA franchise.

text.p: Botswana's national carrier said on Tuesday it opposed South African-based Comair's new franchise with British Airways (BA) on the lucrative route between Gaborone and Johannesburg.
Air Botswana general manager Joshua Galeforolwe said the carrier would suffer.
Comair currently flies the route under its own name but now wants to operate as Comair-BA in Botswana under the British carriers colours after the franchise agreement last year.
Comair's commercial director, Bert van der Linden, said the airlines were discussing the issue.
"We are negotiating with Air Botswana and are getting to a stage where there will be an agreement," he told Reuters.
"They believe because we are waving a BA flag and because of its brand strength it will impinge on their business," van der Linden said.
He added the agreement would be subject to the approval of both Botswana and South African governments.
An agreement in 1993 with the Botswana government allocated a maximum of 1,540 seats a week to both airlines but Air Botswana says it wants more seats because of demand.
"It is a very profitable route...our core route," Galeforolwe told Reuters.
"We are turning away passengers," he added.

Comair's manager in Botswana, John Greyling, said the independent airline normally had seats to spare on its flights, but Air Botswana feared a partnership between Comair and BA would turn the tables and increase competition.
"They will certainly suffer. They fear the name BA, they fear the marketing tool that this franchise places in our hands," Greyling said.
Galeforolwe said Air Botswana objected to a third carrier entering the market.

"The proposed Comair-BA arrangement would be introducing a third national carrier onto the route. The balance of the value of opportunity for Air Botswana could not be equal to that for the other two," he added.
Galeforolwe also said Comair would be violating the original agreement with South African Airways (SAA) which relinquished its rights on the route to Comair five years ago.
Comair operated under contract to SAA, using its own crews and planes, in Comair colours.
Air Botswana was not part of that agreement.

Comair officially joined BA last year on all its routes and pays the British carrier a franchise fee. It uses the image of "the world's favourite airline" and operates as "Comair-British Airways, the largest independent airline in South Africa".
